name: math_least_fixed_point

phase_0.boundary_condition: The complete lattice structure containing the monotone operator domain

VINIT.justification: The initial uninitialized state of the iteration before any application of the operator

TANCH.justification: The universal upper bound that contains all possible fixed points within the lattice

AFWD.justification: The forward transformation that maps an element to its next iteration state

AREV.justification: The descent from a higher lattice point toward the lower fixed point boundary

CLINK.justification: The sequential chaining of operator applications to reach the limit

IMSCRIB.justification: The identity state where the operator recognizes the input as itself

FSPLIT.justification: The branching of a value into a candidate prefixpoint and its subsequent image

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of the candidate set into the unique least fixed point

EVALT.justification: The affirmative condition identifying a prefixpoint

EVALF.justification: The negative condition where the value has not yet reached the prefixpoint set

ENGAGR.justification: The state where a sequence is both a collection of points and a single limit value

IFIX.justification: The permanent fixation of the smallest value that satisfies the identity

phase_3.void_description: The empty set or bottom element before the first iteration
phase_3.true_description: A valid prefixpoint satisfying the Tarski condition
phase_3.false_description: An element that fails the prefixpoint inequality
phase_3.both_description: A limit point existing as both a sequence and a supremum

steps.domain_action: Initialize the process at the lattice bottom element ⊥
Apply the monotone operator f to the current value
Branch the result to evaluate the prefixpoint condition
Confirm the value satisfies f(x) ≤ x
Compose the identity check with the current candidate
Verify the fixed point identity f(x) = x
Recombine the verified identity into the candidate set
Perform a contravariant check against the set of all prefixpoints
Branch to check if this is the minimal element in the set
Reject values that are strictly greater than the infimum
Reconstitute the unique minimal value from the search
Hold the limit state during transfinite iteration if necessary
Permanently record the least fixed point μf in the registry
Close the system within the lattice boundary ⊤

phase_5.memory_mechanism: The set of prefixpoints P = {x | f(x) ≤ x}

phase_6.cycle_cost: One application of the monotone operator f
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The monotonicity ensures the system moves toward a stable equilibrium without loss of information
